title: FleetIO: Managing Multi-Tenant Cloud Storage with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
problem: Cloud virtualized flash storage (SSD) systems must simultaneously support software-isolated and hardware-isolated tenant instances, but face a fundamental tension between performance isolation (preventing noisy neighbors) and resource utilization efficiency — strong isolation wastes storage, while weak isolation causes long-tail latency.
motivation: Multi-tenant cloud SSD platforms have long struggled to jointly achieve performance isolation and high resource utilization, a problem that worsens as workload diversity increases and SSDs become the primary storage substrate.
method: FleetIO assigns each tenant a separate learning agent (using reinforcement learning, where agents improve through trial and error) that learns three coordination tasks: when to process I/O requests, how much storage each tenant gets, and which requests to accept. All agents watch the same system state and coordinate to simultaneously achieve per-tenant performance isolation (preventing noisy neighbors from slowing you down) and efficient overall storage utilization. Since the agents learn automatically rather than relying on hand-tuned policies, the system adapts to changing workloads and jointly optimizes tail latency (the slowest requests) and storage efficiency.
key_novelty: FleetIO replaces hand-tuned storage policies with one learning agent per tenant (software that automatically improves through trial-and-error) that balances giving each tenant isolated, predictable performance with overall storage efficiency, by coordinating through shared system observations.
contributions: FleetIO: a multi-agent RL system for managing multi-tenant cloud flash storage
Joint optimization of performance isolation and resource utilization via MARL
Support for both software-isolated and hardware-isolated storage instance types
Demonstration of adaptive storage management under varying multi-tenant workloads

metrics.other: specific headline numbers not provided in abstract

limitations: MARL training overhead, convergence time, and generalization to unseen workloads not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: multi-agent reinforcement learning for multi-tenant cloud SSD resource management
